## What it finds

An MCP server whose command installs a package each time it starts, with no exact version:

- `npx`, `npm exec`, `pnpm dlx`, `yarn dlx` or `bunx` with a package that has no `@<version>`,
  or only `@latest`, another tag or a range such as `@^1.2.0`;
- `uvx`, `uv tool run` or `pipx run` with a package that has no `==<version>` (also through
  `--from` or `--spec`);
- `docker run` or `podman run` with an image that has no tag, or the `latest` tag, and no
  `@sha256:` digest;
- a git source with no commit.

It reads every agent's MCP config, and the MCP config that installed plugins and extensions
carry. The print names the server and shows the pinned form to write instead.

## Why it matters

An unpinned server runs whatever version was published last, with your permissions, every time
the agent starts. A hijacked maintainer account or a new malicious release reaches you without
anything changing on your disk.

## How to fix

Pin an exact version: `npx -y pkg@1.2.3`, `uvx pkg==1.2.3` (or `uvx --from pkg==1.2.3 cmd`),
`image:1.2.3` or `image@sha256:<digest>`. Choose the version you use now, after reading its
release notes. `agentprint fix` never changes the config: the version is your call.

## Limits

- Local programs and scripts are not packages: `node server.js`, `./bin/server`, `uv run`, and a
  runner such as `npx tsx ./server.ts` that starts a local file are never printed.
- A command built from variables (`${IMAGE}`) is not read.
- A pinned version can still be a bad one: pinning makes a change visible, it does not vouch
  for the code.
